title: 10 Dishes That Explain Pune
description: Ten dishes trace Pune through old-city snacks, fasting food, Camp bakeries, Irani cafés, Parsi kitchens and the city’s own exuberant summer drink.

cards.title: Misal — Bedekar Misal
cards.subtitle: Narayan Peth’s sweet, tangy interpretation
cards.notes: Bedekar’s gravy combines Maharashtrian spices with jaggery and tamarind. It shows how Pune’s misal tradition makes room for sweetness and tang alongside heat.
cards.short_summary: A layered Maharashtrian snack with Bedekar’s distinctive jaggery-and-tamarind gravy.
cards.source_title: Bedekar Misal — Official Website and Misal Story

cards.title: Vada Pav — Garden Vada Pav
cards.subtitle: A Camp street cart with a Pune-specific silhouette
cards.notes: Garden flattens and lengthens its potato vada to cover the specially made pav, then adds coriander chutney and crisp batter fragments. A familiar regional snack becomes unmistakably local through shape and assembly.
cards.short_summary: A broad, flat potato vada tucked into custom-made pav with chutney and crisp batter.
cards.source_title: Condé Nast Traveller India: Is This the Best Vada Pav in Pune?

cards.title: Chutney Sandwich — Marz-o-rin
cards.subtitle: Fast food from Pune’s old Camp storefronts
cards.notes: The café’s direct menu lists this compact white-bread sandwich. Its simplicity—bread and vivid green chutney—recalls the practical refreshments that shaped Camp’s early fast-food culture.
cards.short_summary: Marz-o-rin’s straightforward green-chutney sandwich on white bread.

cards.title: Shrewsbury Biscuit — Kayani Bakery
cards.subtitle: A Camp bakery keeps its firewood ovens working
cards.notes: Kayani has baked Shrewsbury biscuits alongside breads and puffs since its early years. The crisp biscuit connects Pune’s Iranian bakery families, cantonment architecture and enduring appetite for portable gifts.
cards.short_summary: A crisp, buttery biscuit baked at Kayani’s long-running Camp premises.
cards.source_title: The Indian Express: How Pune’s Kayani Bakery Keeps Its Position as a Heritage Landmark

cards.title: Sabudana Khichadi — Appa Khichadi
cards.subtitle: Sago pearls paired with cooling cucumber raita
cards.notes: Appa serves loose-grained sabudana khichadi with kakadi raita, a pairing locally shortened to “khika.” It turns food associated with fasting into an everyday Pune breakfast ritual.
cards.short_summary: Peanut-flecked sabudana khichadi served with cucumber raita.
cards.source_title: The Indian Express: The Making of Appa Chi Khichadi, a Pune Shivratri Favourite

cards.title: Dhansak — Dorabjee and Sons
cards.subtitle: Parsi home cooking at a Camp dining room dating to 1878
cards.notes: Dorabjee’s serves dhansak as part of a remarkably persistent Parsi menu. Lentils, vegetables, spices and meat point to the community history embedded in Pune Cantonment’s everyday restaurants.
cards.short_summary: Parsi lentils and vegetables served with meat and brown rice at Dorabjee’s.
cards.source_title: The Indian Express: Pune Restaurant with the Same Menu Since 1878

cards.title: Bun Maska — Cafe Goodluck
cards.subtitle: An Irani-café breakfast at the edge of Deccan
cards.notes: Goodluck has served buttered buns since 1935, traditionally alongside chai. The combination captures Pune’s Irani cafés as democratic meeting rooms for students, office-goers and long-established regulars.
cards.short_summary: A soft bun spread with butter and paired naturally with chai.
cards.source_title: The Indian Express: Bun and Maska — A Marriage Made Over Tea

cards.title: Mango Mastani — Sujata Mastani
cards.subtitle: A milkshake that behaves like dessert
cards.notes: Sujata thickens milk, pairs it with house-made flavored ice cream and uses seasonal mango as a summer highlight. The layered drink shows Pune turning a modest milk cooler into a city-specific dessert form.
cards.short_summary: Thick mango milk crowned with matching ice cream.
cards.source_title: The Indian Express: Mastani, a Cold Pune Beverage That’s an Ode to Peshwa Bajirao’s Beloved

cards.title: Sajuk Tupatli Biryani — SP’s Biryani House
cards.subtitle: Biryani recast through Maharashtra’s clarified-butter tradition
cards.notes: SP’s identifies sajuk tup—pure ghee—as the defining element of its Maharashtrian approach to biryani. The dish reflects Pune’s habit of absorbing a widely traveled format and giving it a regional accent.
cards.short_summary: A Maharashtrian-style biryani whose defining ingredient is pure ghee.
cards.source_title: The Indian Express: What Made Aamir Khan Recommend This Special Biryani from Pune’s Three-Decade-Old Eatery?

cards.title: Basundi — Durvankur Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: Slow-reduced milk at a Sadashiv Peth dining hall
cards.notes: Durvankur serves basundi, the reduced-milk dessert associated with western Indian celebratory meals. In Pune, it belongs naturally to the dining-hall format: many preparations arriving together rather than a sequence of restaurant courses.
cards.short_summary: A rich reduced-milk dessert served within Pune’s traditional dining-hall culture.
cards.source_title: The Indian Express: Hangout Spots Serve Pune Food Culture on Your Plate
